content.comment_body: Is it possible to create a simple application using [product_name]? I need just a few inputs and outputs. Which model of [product_name] would you recommend? Is there a version without a user interface but with a web server, so I can view screens in a web browser? Can I connect wirelessly and access it from my smartphone? In short, I want to automate a small process and control it via smartphone. What hardware and programming software do I need to purchase?

Hello, It's best to visit the [company_name] [product_name] website and review the online training materials. This will give you experience and help you choose the right [product_name] model. For hardware, I suggest starting with a [product_name] starter kit, which includes everything you need (device, software, cables, and power supply, if required). You can find all relevant information on the official website. Regarding the web server: all modern [product_name] models come with an integrated web server. However, full HMI functionality is limited because web pages are fixed or rely on message text design.

Thanks for the info. I have some experience with [version_no] and panel devices but I'm not sure if [product_name] works similarly. I wish I could enter and monitor product names and quantities from my smartphone browser. Does [product_name] have a database to store data as in STEP 7?

Hello, [product_name] does not offer database storage, but it does have a memory area similar to older PLCs like [version_no], with addresses starting from a certain point. You can refer to other threads or the official [product_name] documentation for more details.

You can connect [product_name] with an operator device to store values as recipes. Another idea is to have [product_name] activate a group of web messages when a product type is selected. Parameters could be chosen using a multiplexer instruction block, for example. One challenge is the inability to customize product description names unless you use identifiers like numbers instead of text. This is a brief explanation and might be a late suggestion, but hopefully it's useful.
Are you referring to the V-memory of the [version_no]? V-memory is sometimes called datablock memory.
The VM area available to users typically ranges from 0.0 to 850.7: Bit: V 0.0 - 850.7 Byte: VB 0-850 Word: VW 0-849 DWord: VD 0-847

Yes, I meant V-memory. My point is that inputs and outputs are mapped at higher addresses, while lower addresses are for network variables, such as flags. So, to directly check inputs, you need to set up communication as you would in STEP 7 or with an operator device, not like with [product_name] of a previous generation. If you have the actual configuration file for the latest [product_name], it should work fine.
Just for academic interest: can the V-memory (VM area) be used to store characters or text strings? Alternatively, can information stored there be displayed on a web page as strings?

As far as I know, that's not possible. The VM area is mainly for transferring digital states (bits) or number values. It supports formats like signed, unsigned, hexadecimal, plus time and date, but not strings.
Thank you, everyone, for sharing your knowledge.
I don't think it's possible to send strings since [product_name] doesn't support string operations or variables.
A new question posted by [user_name] has been moved to its own thread under the subject 'How to create buffer data block in [product_name]?'. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are investigating how [product_name] hardware and its associated software can facilitate small automation projects, focusing on smartphone browser-based monitoring and control via the web server. There is uncertainty regarding data storage options, differences between this system and other PLCs, and web server limitations, especially around customizing displayed information and dynamic content. Users are seeking clarity on how to present descriptive and quantitative data and recognize gaps between available features and their needs.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope [product_name] will offer a customizable web-based user interface accessible from smartphones, options to store and display descriptive data (names, quantities), and straightforward integration of hardware and software.
